title: GraphEdgeV5
description: One typed, directed relation between two nodes of the authorship graph, carrying its own state digest. Edges are what make invalidation computable: each relation declares how a change at one end propagates to the other, so `wi impact` can walk from a changed source to the exact set of claims, paragraphs and release targets that no longer stand — and, just as importantly, to the set that provably still does. Emitted by `Workspace.put_edge()` in `scripts/wi.py`, projected by `build_bundle()` into the `graph/edges.jsonl` member of a `.wiab` bundle, and read by `verify_bundle()` when it checks reference integrity. NOTE ON `illustrates`: it is not `supports`. A media node connected to a meaning node by `illustrates` contributes nothing to that meaning's proof state; it carries invalidation policy `none` precisely so that nothing in a proof can depend on it. A decorative or generated image sitting beside a number reads to a human as evidence for that number, and if that edge could enter a proof closure then a picture becomes a citation. The separation is enforced by the relation type, not by the judgment of whoever wired the graph.

from.description: Logical id of the origin node. Direction is meaningful for every relation in the enum; reversing an edge asserts a different thing.

to.description: Logical id of the target node.

relation.description: Which relation holds, and by implication which invalidation policy governs propagation across it.

state_digest.description: `state_digest()` over the payload `{from, to, relation, payload}` under schema id `graph_edge`. An edge has state because rewiring the graph is itself a change a proof can be stale against.

payload.description: Relation-specific detail: the policy under which a `supports` edge was drawn, the scope of a `qualifies` edge, the reason on a `supersedes` edge. The v5.0 core stores this in the `edge` table's `payload_json` column and writes `{}` for every edge it creates; `build_bundle()` does NOT project it into `graph/edges.jsonl`, so a bundle carries the four required fields only.

logical_id.description: A UUID-shaped, content-derived logical identity produced by `logical_id()`.

digest.description: A SHA-256 digest in the canonical `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` form.

relation.description:
Every edge family defined in references/v5/AUTHORSHIP_GRAPH.md. Invalidation policies, in order of severity: `hard` voids downstream verification immediately; `review` marks downstream state review-required and only a human decision clears it; `soft` annotates without gate consequence; `none` does not propagate at all.

EVIDENTIAL — `supports` (hard), `contradicts` (hard), `qualifies` (hard), `derived_from` (review), `summarizes` (review), `translates` (review), `cites` (hard).

RENDERING AND DEPENDENCY — `renders_as` (review), `asserted_in` (review), `depends_on` (review), `built_from` (hard), `illustrates` (none).

DEFINITIONAL — `defines` (review), `uses_term` (review), `same_meaning_as` (review), `narrows` (review), `broadens` (hard — the most dangerous edit direction).

AUTHORSHIP — `proposed_change_to` (hard), `accepted_by` (hard), `rejected_by` (none), `waived_by` (hard), `invalidates` (hard), `supersedes` (soft).

NARRATIVE — `causes` (review), `precedes` (review), `foreshadows` (soft), `pays_off` (review), `depicts` (soft), `narrates` (review), `signed_by` (hard).

The v5.0 core writes six of these: `supports`, `derived_from`, `supersedes`, `asserted_in`, `renders_as` and `depends_on`. `depends_on` is the generic dependency the impact walker traverses — X `depends_on` Y means a change in Y invalidates X unless X is provably unaffected.
